subject: Post-demo pricing calibration — target $/1M and competitive comps
messages:
From: Ben Yoder <ben@finapps.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Thanks — post-demo volume / budget details

Kimberly / team,

Thanks again for the walkthrough today — the latency and streaming demo looked solid. A few follow-ups from our side re: sizing and budget so you can shape an initial commercial proposal: 

- Our expected usage profile: pilot (months 0–2) ~10M tokens/month, ramp to 30–40M tokens/month by month 6. Spiky weekends (short burst traffic) but steady weekday traffic.
- Budget: for the pilot we have a target spend window of $4k–$8k/month; if the pilot performs we can expand to $10k–$15k/month for scale.
- Procurement preference: 12-month committed term if unit economics align (we prefer a committed seat/volume discount vs pure on-demand).

Two asks: 1) can you share a target $/1M-token range for both on-demand and a 12-month commit? 2) high-level note on any throughput/latency SLA differences for committed capacity.

Would like to get a proposal by early next week so we can align with finance.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Yoder
Head of AI Platform 
FinApps, Inc.

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Ben Yoder <ben@finapps.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com, sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 10:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Thanks — post-demo volume / budget details

Ben — great to meet today. Appreciate the clear volume/budget bands; that helps a lot. High-level response and next steps below.

Quick answers:
- On-demand: our standard hosted on-demand numbers (open models) typically land in the $200–$350 per 1M tokens band depending on model choice and sequence geometry.
- 12-month committed capacity: with a committed volume and a simple ramp profile (pilot -> 30–40M/mo), we can propose a reserved $/1M in the ~$140–$190 range depending on the model family and inference profile. That price assumes a 12-month commit with a monthly minimum and an agreed ramp schedule.
- SLA/throughput: reserved pools give more consistent tail latency and burst credit — we can include a 99th percentile latency target and a burst policy in the SOW.

Next steps:
1) I’ll pull together a short pricing grid (on-demand vs 12mo reserved vs hybrid) with competitor comps (OpenAI, Anthropic, and a couple of open-hosts) and send it to you by EOD Monday.
2) If the grid looks good, we’ll draft a short SOW for the pilot with a clause for conversion to reserved capacity.
3) Please confirm your preferred timeline for procurement and if you need any SOC2/compliance artifacts attached to the SOW.

Looping in Aditya (pricing/ops) and Sean (account lead) so they can build the committed options and competitor benchmarking.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 08:11:00 -0700
Subject: Draft pricing grid & competitor comps (attached)

Team — attaching the initial pricing grid I pulled together for FinApps (pricing_grid_draft.xlsx). Notes from the calc: 

- Volume assumptions used: pilot 10M/mo -> steady 35M/mo.
- Competitor reference points (public list prices we used): OpenAI ~ $340/1M (standard model proxy), Anthropic ~ $270/1M, OpenHostX (optimised quantized) ~ $120/1M.
- Redwood proposals:
  * On-demand (hosted): $320/1M (higher-performance model, non-committed)
  * 12mo reserved (ramp to 35M/mo): $160/1M with a monthly minimum equivalent to 60% of target month in months 1–3 to help cover capacity.
  * Hybrid (pilot on-demand -> reserve conversion): pilot on-demand + credit applied on conversion, effective $190/1M for the first 3 months post-conversion.

Important unit-econ notes: the $/1M is model- and sequence-length dependent — we used a baseline prompt+completion average of 500 tokens per request for the comps. If FinApps uses shorter requests, the effective unit price improves. Additionally, caching/prefix reuse (which their product seems to support) can materially reduce billable tokens; we flagged that for Kimberly to validate with FinApps.

Attachments: pricing_grid_draft.xlsx (spreadsheet with line-item math and comparator links).

Will wait for Kimberly/Sean to approve before we send to the customer.

-Aditya
Aditya Rao
Pricing Lead, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com

- Attachments: pricing_grid_draft.xlsx, SOW_FinApps_draft.pdf.
